q1.a: PentaPrompt is a curated prompt library with copy-ready templates for common work scenarios—writing, coding, marketing, SEO, learning, and video.

q2.q: Which models are these prompts for?
q2.a: Most prompts work well in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. You can also adapt them for other LLMs by adjusting tone, constraints, and output format.

q3.q: How do I use a prompt template?
q3.a: Open a prompt, copy it, and replace placeholders with your context. For best results, add constraints (audience, length, style) and examples.

q1.q: What are writing prompts used for?
q1.a: Use them to generate drafts faster, rewrite with a specific tone, and produce structured outputs like outlines and scripts.

q2.q: How do I avoid generic writing?
q2.a: Add your audience, angle, and constraints. Provide 2–3 examples of style, and ask for multiple variants.

q3.q: Do these work for long-form content?
q3.a: Yes. Start with an outline prompt, then expand section by section with clear constraints and sources.

q1.q: What do SEO prompts help with?
q1.a: They help you plan keyword clusters, create outlines, write meta descriptions, and produce content briefs aligned with search intent.

q2.q: Can AI-written content rank on Google?
q2.a: It can, if it is helpful and accurate. Use prompts to produce structured drafts, then add original insights and verification.

q3.q: How do I make outputs more actionable?
q3.a: Ask for tables, checklists, and step-by-step tasks. Specify target audience, funnel stage, and constraints.

q1.q: Which marketing assets can I generate?
q1.a: Ads, landing page copy, positioning statements, email sequences, and social posts.

q2.q: How do I keep messaging consistent?
q2.a: Provide your brand voice, product positioning, and a few examples. Ask for multiple variants and a final recommended option.

q3.q: What should I include as context?
q3.a: Your audience, offer, benefits, differentiators, objections, and any constraints like length or platform.

q1.q: Are coding prompts safe to use?
q1.a: They are a starting point. Always review code, run tests, and validate security and edge cases.

q2.q: How do I get better code outputs?
q2.a: Provide the stack, constraints, input/output examples, and ask for explanations plus tests.

q3.q: Can I use prompts for refactors?
q3.a: Yes. Ask for step-by-step refactor plans, risk assessment, and incremental changes with tests.

q1.a: They are templates for generating scripts, storyboards, shot lists, and structured instructions for video creation workflows.

q2.q: Which tools can I use them with?
q2.a: Most video prompts are tool-agnostic. You can adapt them for your preferred generator by mapping fields like style, camera, and length.

q3.q: How do I get more consistent results?
q3.a: Specify duration, structure, tone, and visual style. Ask for scene-by-scene outputs and a single global style guide.
